newsitem.title: USA: White House officials, budget chiefs meet Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: White House officials, budget chiefs meet Tuesday.

text.p: Senior White House officials will meet with top congressional budget negotiators for budget negotiations on Tuesday, U.S. officials said on Monday.

Administration officials said the White House was expected to be represented by Office of Management and Budget Director Frank Raines, National Economic Council Chairman Gene Sperling and senior White House legislative director John Hilley.

Congressional aides said Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici of New Mexico and House Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich of Ohio, both Republicans, would attend the meeting, as would the ranking Democrats on the committees.
None of the officials would state the exact time or place for the meeting, although one said it was expected to occur during the afternoon on Capitol Hill.

During the congressional recess over the past two weeks there have been a series of staff-level meetings between the White House and congressional budget experts, but the top officials have not been involved.
"This is the beginning of serious negotiations," said one administration official who asked not to be identified.

The official said he was drawing a distinction not merely between this meeting and the recent staff talks, but also between it and the many meetings held since President Bill Clinton submitted his fiscal year 1998 budget in February.
There appears to have been little progress in the talks since then.

In an effort to revive the discussions, Clinton invited the budget chairmen to the White House in mid-March and last week Hilley told reporters Clinton was expected to meet with the Congressional leaders during the week of April 14.
Earlier on Monday, Republican Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott told reporters such a meeting might slip past next week, but an administration official said next week remained "a possibility."
